record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: For each integer k ≥ 2, either find a chiral 4k-polytope whose right Petrie paths and left Petrie paths have different lengths, or prove that no such chiral 4k-polytope exists.

evidence.quote: Problem 10 Find examples of chiral 4k-polytopes (where k ≥ 2) with the property that the length of the right Petrie paths does not coincide with the length of the left Petrie paths, or prove their non-existence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank n is a partially ordered set (with elements called faces, ranked from -1 to n) satisfying the standard axioms of abstract polytopes: it has a unique minimum face and unique maximum face, every maximal chain (flag) has exactly n+2 elements, it is strongly flag-connected, and it satisfies the diamond condition. Such a polytope is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags, with adjacent flags lying in different orbits.

For a chiral polytope P of rank n with base flag Φ = {F_{-1}, F_0, …, F_n}, let σ_1, …, σ_{n-1} be the standard generators of the rotation subgroup of Aut(P), where σ_i fixes all faces of Φ except F_{i-1} and F_i. The right Petrie path and the left Petrie path of P are the orbits of the base flag under the cyclic groups generated, respectively, by the "right" Petrie automorphism π_R = σ_1 σ_2 ⋯ σ_{n-1} and the "left" Petrie automorphism π_L = σ_1 σ_2^{-1} σ_3 σ_4^{-1} ⋯ (with alternating signs). The lengths of the right Petrie path and left Petrie path are the orders of π_R and π_L respectively.

For each integer k ≥ 2, either exhibit a chiral abstract polytope of rank 4k whose right Petrie paths and left Petrie paths have different lengths, or prove that for every chiral abstract polytope of rank 4k these two lengths must coincide.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turn up the general theory of left/right Petrie polygons of chiral polytopes and various constructions of chiral 4-polytopes, but no result was found that either constructs a chiral 4k-polytope (k ≥ 2) with unequal left and right Petrie path lengths or proves these lengths must always coincide. The problem appears to remain unresolved in the publicly available literature.

status_evidence.title: Chiral Polyhedra in 3-Dimensional Geometries and from a Petrie–Coxeter Construction
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Petrie-type constructions arising from chiral and regular polytopes but does not resolve the rank-4k Petrie length question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on Petrie constructions for chiral polytopes does not address the equality of left/right Petrie path lengths in rank 4k.

status_evidence.snippet: Bibliographic compendium for the theory of abstract chiral polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference list on chiral polytopes; no entry reports settling the 4k Petrie path length problem.
